g.text: Repaired accuracy approaches the FP32 quantization limit

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: middle; fill: #444444

g.text: Reference values use exact integer division and nearest-even rounding over every input significand

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Subnormal rounding uses the high-precision NR result directly, with one nearest-even rounding and no intermediate FP32 rounding.

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: For x = 0x7f7ffffc, Z3 proves that no finite FP32 output can meet 9e-8 relative error. The normal-core target cannot cover all normal inputs.
